title: Protocol for a Mixed-Methods Feasibility Study of a Smoking Cessation App
author: Farhan Alanazi

steps.title: Recruit and Screen Participants
steps.instruction: Recruit 40–50 university students from a higher education institution in Saudi Arabia using convenience sampling via social media platforms (WhatsApp and Telegram).

substeps.instruction: Administer a screening form to interested students.

Verify eligibility: aged 18 years or older, currently enrolled university students, smoke at least five cigarettes per day, own a smartphone with internet access, and able to provide informed consent.

Apply exclusion criteria: current enrollment in another structured smoking cessation program, medical conditions requiring supervised smoking cessation, inability to provide informed consent/understand procedures, or visual/cognitive impairments limiting app engagement.

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent and Baseline Data
steps.instruction: Enroll eligible participants and collect initial quantitative measurements.

substeps.instruction: Provide the Participant Information Sheet and Consent Form to eligible students.
Assess baseline nicotine dependence using the Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence (FTND).
Collect baseline exploratory smoking-related outcomes, including cigarettes per day (CPD) and 7-day point prevalence abstinence (PPA).

steps.title: Implement UniQuit Intervention
steps.instruction: Have participants use the UniQuit AI- and gamification-based smoking cessation app prototype for a duration of 6 weeks.

substeps.instruction: Ensure participants have access to app features: Daily Missions, Craving Help, AI Quit Coach, tailored reminders, progress tracking, Health Credits, badges, stress support, relapse support, and anonymous peer support.

Provide general supportive guidance via the AI Quit Coach (informed by WHO clinical treatment guidelines for tobacco cessation in adults), ensuring no diagnosis, prescribing, or individualized medical treatment advice is given.

steps.title: Collect Post-Intervention Data
steps.instruction: Gather quantitative and qualitative data following the 6-week intervention period.

substeps.instruction: Collect post-intervention quantitative data to assess feasibility outcomes, usability, and exploratory smoking-related outcomes (CPD and 7-day PPA).
Conduct semi-structured interviews with a subset of participants to explore acceptability, usability, perceived usefulness, and barriers/facilitators to engagement.
Audio-record interviews with consent, then transcribe and anonymize the recordings.

steps.title: Analyze Study Data
steps.instruction: Perform descriptive and thematic analysis on the collected data sets.

substeps.instruction: Analyze quantitative data descriptively using frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations.
Compare changes in CPD from baseline to post-intervention using paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests based on data distribution.
Summarize 7-day PPA at post-intervention using frequencies and percentages.
Analyze qualitative interview data thematically using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis approach.
